guard: the managed row keeps the process fact and the mesh fact separate, never prints `working` as a bare word, parenthesises the role, and reports uptime in minutes
why: The suite imports formatManagedRow from src through tsx, so a mutation is seen without a build and needs no rebuild after the restore.
Each mutation is compile-clean and its anchor occurs exactly once in the named file.

mutations.name: S1 presence `working` reaches the operator as a bare word
mutations.find: const mesh = a.mesh === "working" ? "working · progress unknown" : a.mesh;
mutations.expectRed: a working seat renders `mesh working · progress unknown`
mutations.cell: a working seat renders `mesh working · progress unknown`
mutations.note: `working` alone claims progress the manager never reported; the qualifier is the whole point of the row.

mutations.name: S2 the row drops the role from its name/role label
mutations.expectRed: the row leads with the peer's name/role label
mutations.cell: the row leads with the peer's name/role label
mutations.note: Without the parentheses a role is indistinguishable from a second name field.

mutations.name: S3 uptime is divided by the wrong unit
mutations.expectRed: uptime is rounded to whole minutes
mutations.cell: uptime is rounded to whole minutes
mutations.note: The cell's only fixture is an exact 5 minutes, so it cannot separate round from floor or truncation; a wrong divisor is what it does catch. The boundary case is unproven and is recorded as a follow-up.
